turns.zh: 感谢。

transcript.sec: Reflections on Luca and CEO Integrity

turns.en: Okay. I thought Luca was really interesting. His company's doing really well and the guy beats to his own drummer. Just to stick on the ending there. I mean, for CEOs, integrity is really an underrated thing. Uh, you are what your word is. You've got a great reputation probably, but you do one stupid thing and you can kind of have that crash down. So, I like that. I like that he's like, I never lie and I never omit important info. And he could have just said that and I'd be like, that's a bunch of BS, but I had three of the companies he acquired kind of say the same thing. It reminds me of my last interview with Ali Goi from Data Bricks where he's like the worst thing you can be as a CEO is conflict averse and like if you're never going to admit important information when talking to someone, you're going to have conflict. And so that just sort of reinforces that in my mind.
turns.zh: 好的。我觉得 Luca 真的很有趣。他的公司做得非常好，而且这个人特立独行。就接着结尾那里说。我的意思是，对 CEO 来说，诚信真的是一个被低估的东西。你就是你的话。你可能名声很好，但你做一件蠢事，就可能崩塌。所以，我喜欢这一点。我喜欢他说，我从不撒谎，也从不隐瞒重要信息。他本可以就这么说，我会觉得那是一堆废话，但他收购的三家公司都说了同样的话。这让我想起我上次采访 Data Bricks 的 Ali Goi 时，他说作为 CEO 最糟糕的就是回避冲突，如果你在与人交谈时从不承认重要信息，你就会产生冲突。所以这在我脑海中强化了这一点。

turns.en: Other things I really thought were unique was like the way he does hiring is really unique along a lot of different levels. I mean, he's very conscious about the top of his funnel and how he brings people in. is very conscious about his employee brand. This does rhyme with HubSpot. We we had a woman named Katie Burke who who she was a marketer actually that we moved into run HR and she was excellent at it and she treated it like marketing like how do we how do we how do we create a flywheel? How do we pull people in and create a real employee brand and now she's the COO actually at Harvey. Uh, but I think that's really important for scaling companies. Create a a hiring brand. Getting very good at hiring, I think, is important. He's got a whole darn data science team looking at hundreds or thousands of signals, trying to find the right candidates, and sounds like he does lots of interesting things in that process. One of the least interesting things it sounds like he does is the interview itself. I kind of agree with that. Like when I interview, everyone's good at being interviewed now. And so I discount that a little bit relative to other signals. So I thought that was I thought that was pretty interesting.
turns.zh: 我觉得其他真正独特的地方是他招聘的方式在很多不同层面上都非常独特。我的意思是，他非常注重漏斗顶端以及如何引进人才。非常注重他的雇主品牌。这与 HubSpot 有相似之处。我们有一位叫 Katie Burke 的女性，她实际上是营销人员，我们让她负责人力资源，她非常擅长，她像做营销一样对待它，比如我们如何创造一个飞轮？我们如何吸引人才并创建一个真正的雇主品牌，现在她实际上是 Harvey 的 COO。但我认为这对扩张中的公司非常重要。创建一个招聘品牌。非常擅长招聘，我认为很重要。他有一整个数据科学团队，研究数百或数千个信号，试图找到合适的候选人，听起来他在这个过程中做了很多有趣的事情。听起来他做的最不有趣的事情之一就是面试本身。我有点同意。就像我面试时，现在每个人都擅长面试。所以相对于其他信号，我对此打折扣。所以我觉得那相当有趣。

turns.en: I mean he's pretty obsessive on talent. He you know he said it he said it on this pod. I've heard him say it other times like you just can't drop the bar. And like as companies scale they they inevitably do drop the bar. And it sounds like he really hasn't and he's stuck on that and it causes a lot of suffering and a lot of people working very long hours. Uh but he he sticks with that. Um, and you know, he weighed in on the the age-old battle that I hear from CEOs all the time. Should I hire for experience or slope? And he's at a pretty big scale and he's still like full-on slope over experience. I think his management teams probably other than his founders are all in their 20s uh, and have high slope and it's working for him. I'm not saying that's the answer. I think for some people experience matters. also buys a lot of companies in the in like the PLG type sales motion where you know it's not necessarily enterprise sales or maybe some experience might be useful but that's where he comes in on that he talks so much about team team but then at one point he's like actually you can have a mediocre team if your strategy is really good which I thought hurt my head a little bit and then he also talked about when he buys a company is it more his picking or his operating so operating you know he's a really good operator I think the reality is you have to be really good at all of that stuff. You need to have a really compelling strategy and that's unique relative to your competitors and is compelling to your potential customers. You need to be an amazing operator and you need to have an amazing team. There's not really any shortcut on any of that stuff. Anyway, that's Luca. I thought he was really interesting and smart and I hope you liked it.
turns.zh: 我的意思是，他对人才非常执着。你知道，他在这期播客上说过。我听过他在其他时候也说过，你就是不能降低标准。而随着公司扩张，他们不可避免地会降低标准。听起来他并没有，他坚持这一点，这导致了很多痛苦和很多人长时间工作。但他坚持这一点。而且，你知道，他谈到了我经常从 CEO 那里听到的古老争论。我应该招聘经验还是潜力？他公司规模相当大，但他仍然完全倾向于潜力而非经验。我认为他的管理团队，除了创始人之外，可能都是 20 多岁，潜力很高，这对他有效。我不是说这就是答案。我认为对一些人来说经验很重要。他还收购了很多公司，采用 PLG 类型的销售模式，你知道，不一定是企业销售，也许一些经验可能有用，但这就是他的观点。他大谈特谈团队，但有一次他说，实际上如果你的战略真的很好，你可以有一个平庸的团队，我觉得这有点让我头疼。然后他还谈到，当他收购一家公司时，更多的是他的挑选还是他的运营，所以是运营。你知道，他是一个非常优秀的运营者。我认为现实是你必须在所有这些方面都非常出色。你需要有一个非常引人注目的战略，相对于竞争对手独特，并且对潜在客户有吸引力。你需要成为一个出色的运营者，你需要有一个出色的团队。这些事情真的没有捷径。总之，这就是 Luca。我觉得他非常有趣和聪明，我希望你喜欢。
